applies_why: The judge text issues an UNDERDETERMINED verdict and states the ground for it, so K-S2's restriction on grounds for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED is in scope.
quote: D5 vs C1 (Acts 2:30): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] and [CR3] answered the loins/seed row with Genesis 46:26 and Hebrews 7:10 (loins at depth) and the legal/flesh distinction, while [DR3] presses that the only named Davidic man is Joseph; neither chain forces the other.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: single verse does not state a link or its contrary — two readings: it forbids any underdetermination resting on a verse's silence, or only an explicit single-verse non-statement ground; I used the latter.
why: The judge rests UNDERDETERMINED on the two chains not forcing each other, not on the single verse's failure to state the link or its contrary, so it does not breach K-S2.
